title: Identification of genomic features that uniquely impact estrogen receptor alpha binding and its effects on gene expression in endometrial cancer.
authors: Richey, Alexandra; Kitchen, Noel; Rush, Craig M; Vahrenkamp, Jeffery M; Abewe, Hosiana; Osbourne, Kyle S; Bott, Alex J; Dalley, Brian K; Rutter, Jared; Gertz, Jason
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习预测子宫内膜癌中ER（ESR1）的基因组结合与基因表达效应，聚焦ERE基序及染色质特征，属广义TF-DNA互作结合位点预测，但未涉及三维结构建模或分子动力学模拟，方法深度有限。
abstract: Estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1, also known as estrogen receptor alpha or ER) is an established oncogenic transcription factor in breast and endometrial cancer; however, more is known about the mechanisms controlling ER behavior in breast cancer, and therapies targeting ER have been much more successful in breast cancer. To address this disparity, we characterize the genomic features that control ER in endometrial cancer and determine to what extent these factors differ from those in breast cancer. We focus on the locations of estrogen response elements (EREs), ER's preferred DNA-binding motif, throughout the human genome. To identify factors that predict ER genomic binding and effects on target gene expression, we apply machine learning to genomic data for each ERE in Ishikawa cells (ER-positive endometrial cancer) and T-47D cells (ER-positive breast cancer). Many of these factors, such as chromatin accessibility and histone modifications, are predictive of ER activity in both cell lines. However, the transcription factors that predict ER activity are cell type specific, including FOXA1 and GATA3 in T-47D cells and ETV4 and SOX17 in Ishikawa cells. In addition, the features that predict ER binding and effects on gene expression differ, with transcription at EREs in the absence of estrogen being predictive of ER regulatory activity. A CRISPR knockout screen in Ishikawa cells, as well as follow-up experiments, confirms the discovery that SOX17 controls ER activity in endometrial cancer cells. These results identify important genomic features of ER binding and regulatory activity and how these features differ between endometrial cancer and breast cancer cells.
abstract_zh: 雌激素受体1（ESR1，也称为雌激素受体α或ER）是乳腺癌和子宫内膜癌中公认的致癌转录因子；然而，关于控制ER在乳腺癌中行为的机制了解得更多，且靶向ER的疗法在乳腺癌中取得了更大的成功。为解决这一差异，我们表征了控制子宫内膜癌中ER的基因组特征，并确定这些因素与乳腺癌中的差异程度。我们聚焦于雌激素反应元件（EREs）——ER的首选DNA结合基序——在整个人类基因组中的位置。为识别预测ER基因组结合及其对靶基因表达影响的因子，我们将机器学习应用于Ishikawa细胞（ER阳性子宫内膜癌）和T-47D细胞（ER阳性乳腺癌）中每个ERE的基因组数据。许多这些因子，如染色质可及性和组蛋白修饰，在两种细胞系中均能预测ER活性。然而，预测ER活性的转录因子具有细胞类型特异性，包括T-47D细胞中的FOXA1和GATA3，以及Ishikawa细胞中的ETV4和SOX17。此外，预测ER结合及其对基因表达影响的特征有所不同，其中在无雌激素情况下ERE处的转录可预测ER调控活性。在Ishikawa细胞中进行的CRISPR敲除筛选以及后续实验证实了SOX17控制子宫内膜癌细胞中ER活性的发现。这些结果识别了ER结合和调控活性的重要基因组特征，以及这些特征在子宫内膜癌和乳腺癌细胞之间的差异。
